hindi: उन छह रसों की योनि जल है। छेदन और उपशमन, ये दो कर्म हैं; उन दोनों के मिश्रण से साधारणता होती है। स्वादुता और अस्वादुता रुचि है; हित और अहित प्रभाव हैं। आश्रय तो पाँच महाभूतों के विकार हैं, जो प्रकृति, विकृति, विचार, देश और काल के अधीन हैं। द्रव्य नाम वाले उन आश्रयों में गुरु, लघु, शीत, उष्ण, स्निग्ध, रूक्ष आदि गुण होते हैं। क्षरण के कारण क्षार (कहलाता है); वह रस नहीं है; वह द्रव्य है, जो अनेक रसों से उत्पन्न, अनेक रसों वाला, अधिकतर कटु और लवण, अनेक इन्द्रियार्थों से युक्त और करण से निर्मित है। रसों की अव्यक्तता तो प्रकृति में, अथवा अनुरस रूप या अनुरस से युक्त द्रव्य में होती है। फिर, उन आश्रय आदि भावों के विशेषों के असंख्येय होने के कारण (रसों की) असंख्येयता ठीक नहीं है; क्योंकि इन आश्रय आदि भावों में से एक-एक भी विशेषों को ग्रहण करता है, क्योंकि विशेष असंख्येय हैं, और उससे (रस का) अन्यत्व सिद्ध नहीं होता, क्योंकि ये अधिकतर परस्पर संसृष्ट रहते हैं; और उत्पत्ति के कारण इन गुणप्रकृति वालों की असंख्येयता नहीं होती। इसलिए बुद्धिमान् संसृष्ट रसों का कर्म नहीं बताते।
english: Of these six tastes the source is water. Cutting and pacifying are the two actions; from the mixing of the two comes commonness (sādhāraṇatva). Palatability and unpalatability are (a matter of) liking (bhakti); wholesome and unwholesome are the effects (prabhāva). The substrata (āśraya), however, are modifications of the five great elements, dependent on nature, modification, vicāra, place and time. In these substrata, called substances (dravya), are the qualities (guṇa) heavy, light, cold, hot, unctuous, dry and the rest. Alkali (kṣāra) is so called from wearing away (kṣaraṇa); it is not a taste: it is a substance, produced from many tastes, having many tastes, mostly pungent and salty, accompanied by many sense-objects, produced by a process (karaṇa). Unmanifestness of the tastes, however, occurs in their source (prakṛti), or in a substance that is a subsidiary taste (anurasa) or is accompanied by a subsidiary taste. Again, countlessness (of the tastes) because the particulars of those entities, the substrata and the rest, are countless is not proper: for each one of these entities, the substrata and the rest, takes on particulars, since particulars are countless, and otherness (of taste) does not follow from that, because they are for the most part combined with one another; nor does countlessness arise, from their production, for these (tastes) whose nature is qualities. Therefore the intelligent do not teach the action of combined tastes.

text_flags.why: 'aparisaṃkhyeyeatva' is not a form (stray e before atva); the same compound is printed correctly as viśeṣāparisaṃkhyeyatvāt later in this unit
'veśeṣa' is not a word; viśeṣa (particular) is the word used throughout this unit (viśeṣāparisaṃkhyeyatvāt in the same sentence)

notes: The unit answers the views of units 8 and P1 to P7 point by point (water, cutting/pacifying, commonness, palatability, wholesomeness, the five elements, the qualities, kṣāra, avyakta, countlessness). vicāra in prakṛtivikṛtivicāra- is kept in Sanskrit: its sense here (consideration, combination or processing) is not certain from the chunk. prakṛti 'source' may refer to the source water named at the start of the unit or to the original state; anurase may mean 'in (a substance where the taste is only) subsidiary'. The attachment of parasparasaṃsṛṣṭabhūyiṣṭhatvāt is ambiguous: it is taken as the reason for 'otherness does not follow'; it can also be read as the reason for the following clause. guṇaprakṛtīnām is taken as a bahuvrīhi 'whose nature is qualities' agreeing with eṣām (the tastes); a reading 'of the qualities and natures' is possible, so this clause is uncertain. karaṇa 'process' = preparation by a procedure; the ';' attached to karaṇābhinirvṛttam is left out of the split.

hindi: किन्तु पहले तो द्रव्यों के भेद को लक्ष्य करके हम कुछ कहेंगे।

hindi: इस प्रसंग में सब द्रव्य पाञ्चभौतिक है; वह चेतन और अचेतन है। उसके गुण शब्द आदि और गुरु आदि से लेकर द्रव तक हैं; कर्म पाँच प्रकार का कहा गया है, वमन आदि।
english: In this context every substance is made of the five elements (pāñcabhautika); it is sentient and insentient. Its qualities are sound and the rest, and heavy and the rest ending with fluid (drava); action is stated to be fivefold, emesis and the rest.

text_flags.why: sarvā (f.) does not agree with dravyaṃ (n.); sarvaṃ dravyaṃ gives the agreement the sentence needs
'acenam' is not a word; acetanam (insentient) is the counterpart of cetanāvat in the same phrase (cetanāvad ... ca)
possible: qualities 'ending with dravya (substance)' gives no sense, since a substance is not a quality; drava (fluid) is a quality, listed among the qualities in unit 11 (dravasnighda...)

notes: pāñcabhautika is a derived word, not split. The dravyāntāḥ flag is only possible: the printed form may also be read as 'qualities that end in (inhere in) substance', which is strained.

hindi: उनमें जो द्रव्य गुरु, खर, कठिन, मन्द, स्थिर, विशद, सान्द्र, स्थूल और गन्ध गुणों की बहुलता वाले हैं, वे पार्थिव हैं; वे उपचय, संघात, गुरुता और स्थिरता करते हैं। जो द्रव, स्निग्ध, शीत, मन्द, मृदु, पिच्छिल और रस गुणों की बहुलता वाले हैं, वे आप्य हैं; वे उपक्लेद, स्नेह, बन्ध, विष्यन्द, मृदुता और प्रसन्नता करते हैं। जो उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, सूक्ष्म, लघु, रूक्ष, विशद और रूप गुणों की बहुलता वाले हैं, वे आग्नेय हैं; वे दाह, पाक, प्रभा, प्रकाश और वर्ण करते हैं। जो लघु, शीत, रूक्ष, खर, विशद, सूक्ष्म और स्पर्श गुणों की बहुलता वाले हैं, वे वायव्य हैं; वे रूक्षता, ग्लानि, विचरण, विशदता और लघुता करते हैं। जो मृदु, लघु, सूक्ष्म, श्लक्ष्ण और शब्द गुणों की बहुलता वाले हैं, वे आकाशात्मक हैं; वे मृदुता, सुषिरता और लघुता करते हैं।
english: Among them, substances abounding in the qualities heavy, rough, hard, slow, stable, non-slimy, dense, gross and smell are earthy (pārthiva); they produce increase (upacaya), compactness, heaviness and stability. Those abounding in the qualities fluid, unctuous, cold, slow, soft, slimy and taste are watery (āpya); they produce moistening (upakleda), unctuousness, binding, liquefaction (viṣyanda), softness and refreshment. Those abounding in the qualities hot, sharp, subtle, light, dry, non-slimy and form (rūpa) are fiery (āgneya); they produce burning, pāka (cooking, digestion), lustre, light and colour. Those abounding in the qualities light, cold, dry, rough, non-slimy, subtle and touch are airy (vāyavya); they produce dryness, weariness (glāni), movement (vicāra), non-sliminess and lightness. Those abounding in the qualities soft, light, subtle, smooth and sound are of the nature of space (ākāśa); they produce softness, porosity and lightness.

text_flags.why: 'snighda' is a transposition; snigdha (unctuous) is the quality word (printed snigdha in unit P8, gurulaghuśītoṣṇasnigdharūkṣādyāḥ)

'sgneha' is not a word (sneha, unctuousness, the action matching snigdha); 'mārda' is not a word: mārdava (softness), printed mārdava in the last clause of this unit, matches the quality mṛdu of the same list

notes: Prose (typed as 'verse'). upakleda is rendered 'moistening' (the action of the watery substances), distinct from kleda. pāka of fiery substances is kept Sanskrit ('cooking, digestion'). vicāra of airy substances is taken as 'movement' (literally 'moving about'). rūpa, sparśa, śabda, gandha, rasa are the sense-qualities form, touch, sound, smell and taste.

hindi: इस उपदेश के अनुसार जगत् में कोई द्रव्य ऐसा नहीं मिलता जो औषध न हो, उस-उस युक्ति और उस-उस प्रयोजन को लक्ष्य करके।
english: By this teaching, no substance is found in the world that is not a medicine, with regard to this or that rational planning (yukti) and this or that purpose.
notes: Prose (typed as 'verse'). nānauṣadhibhūtam is split na + anauṣadhibhūtam ('not non-medicine'); the double negation gives 'no substance ... that is not a medicine'. A split nānā-auṣadhibhūtam ('various medicines') does not fit the sentence.

through the power of substance and qualities
words.gram: m. abl. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: किन्तु द्रव्य केवल गुणों के प्रभाव से ही कार्यकारी नहीं होते; क्योंकि द्रव्य, द्रव्य के प्रभाव से, गुणों के प्रभाव से और द्रव्य तथा गुणों के प्रभाव से, उस-उस काल में, उस-उस अधिकरण को पाकर, उस-उस युक्ति और उस-उस प्रयोजन को लक्ष्य करके जो करते हैं, वह कर्म है; जिससे करते हैं, वह वीर्य है; जहाँ करते हैं, वह अधिकरण है; जब करते हैं, वह काल है; जैसे करते हैं, वह उपाय है; जो सिद्ध करते हैं, वह फल है।
english: But substances are not effective only through the power (prabhāva) of their qualities alone; for what substances do, through the power of the substance, through the power of the qualities, and through the power of substance and qualities, at this or that time, having reached this or that site, with regard to this or that rational planning (yukti) and this or that purpose, that is action (karma); that by which they do it is potency (vīrya); where they do it is the site (adhikaraṇa); when they do it is the time (kāla); how they do it is the means (upāya); what they accomplish is the result (phala).

text_flags.why: 'ṭam' is not a word; the phrase tāṃ tāṃ yuktim is printed in unit 12 (tāṃ tāṃ yuktimarthaṃ ca taṃ tam), and the feminine tām agrees with yuktim
'kuvanti' is not a form; kurvanti is printed five times in this unit in the same yat/yena/yatra... series

notes: Prose (typed as 'verse'). kevalam and eva are both rendered ('only ... alone'); together they make one restrictive claim. āsādya: absolutive of ā-√sad (causative form 'having reached').

words.gloss: through the power of substance, place and time
words.gram: m. abl. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: और इन (रसों) का भेद, जिसके तिरसठ प्रकार के विकल्प हैं, द्रव्य, देश और काल के प्रभाव से होता है; उसका हम उपदेश करेंगे।
english: And the division of these (tastes), with sixty-three kinds of gradation (vikalpa), comes about through the power of substance, place and time; we shall teach it.
notes: Prose (typed as 'verse'). eṣām is taken as 'of these (tastes)', the topic of the chapter.

hindi: मधुर, अम्ल आदि के साथ, और अम्ल आदि शेष (रसों) के साथ पृथक्-पृथक् योग को प्राप्त होते हैं; ये पन्द्रह द्रव्य दो रसों वाले हैं।
english: Sweet with sour and the rest, and sour and the rest with the remaining ones, go separately into combination; these are the fifteen substances of two tastes.
notes: svādu here is the taste 'sweet'. The singular svāduḥ and plural amlādayaḥ share the plural verb yānti. COUNT: 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 15 pairs.

words.gloss: joined with sour and the rest

hindi: मधुर का, अम्ल आदि से पृथक्-पृथक् युक्त होकर, शेष (रसों) के साथ पृथक् योग होता है; उसी प्रकार अम्ल का, लवण का, और उसी प्रकार कटु का।
english: Sweet, joined separately with sour and the rest, would combine separately with the remaining ones; likewise sour, salty and likewise pungent.
notes: SENTENCE (no regrouping needed): units 16 and 17 are one sentence (the twenty three-taste substances). COUNT: 10 + 6 + 3 + 1 = 20, as stated in unit 17.

hindi: तीन रसों वाले द्रव्य संख्या के क्रम से बीस कहे गए हैं; और चार (रसों) के समूह से दस और पाँच द्रव्य कहे जाएँगे।
english: substances of three tastes, in due number, are stated as twenty; and ten and five substances will be told by the set of four (tastes).

text_flags.why: 'sṃ' (anusvāra with no vowel) is not possible; yathāsaṃkhyam (in due number) is the word, and the metre needs the vowel a (8 syllables in the first quarter)

notes: vakṣyante is taken as future passive ('will be told'); the form is also the middle future 'they will tell'.

words.gloss: by the count of four-taste sets

hindi: मधुर और अम्ल साथ मिलकर, लवण आदि के साथ पृथक्-पृथक् योग को प्राप्त होकर, शेष (रसों) के साथ पृथक् योग को प्राप्त होते हैं, चार रसों की संख्या के अनुसार।
english: Sweet and sour together, having gone separately into combination with salty and the rest, go separately into combination with the remaining ones, by the count of four tastes.

text_flags.why: 'gattau' is not a form; gatau (nom. du. ppp. √gam, agreeing with svādvamlau ... sahitau) fits the grammar

notes: COUNT: sweet and sour with two of the remaining four = 6 four-taste substances.

hindi: उसी प्रकार मधुर और लवण साथ मिलकर, कटु आदि से पृथक्-पृथक् युक्त होकर, शेष (रसों) के साथ पृथक् योग को प्राप्त होते हैं; उसी प्रकार मधुर और कटु।
english: Likewise sweet and salty together, joined separately with pungent and the rest, go separately into combination with the remaining ones; so too sweet and pungent (ūṣaṇa).
notes: ūṣaṇa is a synonym of kaṭu (pungent) here. COUNT: sweet and salty 3, sweet and pungent 1.

hindi: अम्ल और लवण साथ मिलकर, कटु आदि से पृथक्-पृथक् युक्त होकर, शेष (रसों) के साथ पृथक् योग को प्राप्त होते हैं; उसी प्रकार अम्ल और कटु शेष (रसों) के साथ।
english: Sour and salty together, joined separately with pungent and the rest, go separately into combination with the remaining ones; likewise sour and pungent with the remaining ones.
notes: COUNT: sour and salty 3, sour and pungent 1.

hindi: और तिक्त सहित लवण और कटु कषाय के साथ युक्त होते हैं। और एक-एक को छोड़ देने से पाँच रसों वाले (द्रव्य) छह कहे गए हैं।
english: And salty and pungent (ūṣaṇa), together with bitter, are joined with astringent. And they say there are six (substances) of five tastes, by leaving out each one.
notes: The singular yujyate has the dual subject lavaṇoṣaṇau; the dual would be yujyete, which the metre would also allow. This is noted, not flagged, since the chunk gives no other evidence. COUNT: 6 + 3 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 15 four-taste substances (units 18 to 21), as stated in unit 17.

hindi: और एक रस वाले (द्रव्य) छह होते हैं, और छह रसों वाला एक ही; इस प्रकार रसों की संख्या के अनुसार द्रव्यों के तिरसठ (भेद) बताए गए हैं।
english: And there are six of one taste, and just one of six tastes; thus sixty-three (kinds) of substances are indicated by the count of tastes.
notes: COUNT: 15 + 20 + 15 + 6 + 6 + 1 = 63. The Hindi 'ही' renders eva with ekam.

words.gram: f. nom. sg., negated gerundive (kṛtya) sam-√khyā

words.gloss: by the reckoning of tastes and subsidiary tastes
words.gram: n. abl. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: किन्तु रस और अनुरस की कल्पना से तिरसठ (की संख्या) असंख्येय हो जाती है; क्योंकि रस तर और तम (भेदों) के द्वारा उस संख्या को पार कर जाते हैं।
english: But the sixty-three would become countless through the reckoning of tastes and subsidiary tastes (anurasa); for the tastes, by degrees of 'more' and 'most' (tara, tama), go beyond that count.
notes: tara and tama are the comparative and superlative suffixes, used as nouns for degrees of intensity; taratama may also be read as a neuter dvandva.

words.gloss: by those who reflect on tastes

hindi: संयोग सत्तावन हैं, किन्तु कल्पना तिरसठ प्रकार की है; वहाँ रसों की योग्यता के कारण रस का चिन्तन करने वालों ने (इसे) कल्पित किया है।
english: The combinations are fifty-seven, but the arrangement (kalpanā) is sixty-threefold; it has been devised by those who reflect on tastes, because of the suitability of the tastes there.
notes: fifty-seven = the combinations of two or more tastes (15 + 20 + 15 + 6 + 1); with the 6 single tastes the arrangement is 63 (unit 22). tatra 'there' is taken as 'in that matter' (in the arrangement or its use).

words.gram: m. acc. pl., bahuvrīhi with dvandva

hindi: सिद्धि चाहने वाले वैद्य को दोष, औषध आदि का विचार करके कहीं एक रस की कल्पना करनी चाहिए और कहीं संयुक्त रसों की।
english: A physician who desires success, after considering doṣa, medicine and the rest, is to employ a single taste in some cases and combined tastes in others.

text_flags.why: 'aiṣadha' is not a word; doṣa + auṣadha (medicine) gives doṣauṣadha by sandhi, and the line keeps 16 syllables either way

words.gloss: of two tastes and the rest

hindi: बुद्धिमान् रोगों के प्रति दो रसों आदि वाले द्रव्यों की, और संयुक्त रसों की, अथवा एक-एक रस की भी कल्पना करते हैं।
english: The wise employ, against diseases, substances of two tastes and the rest, and combined tastes, or also tastes one by one.
notes: vā api is rendered 'or also' (Hindi अथवा ... भी).

words.gloss: knower of the gradations of tastes
knower of the gradations of doṣas

hindi: जो रसों के विकल्पों का ज्ञाता हो और दोषों के विकल्पों का ज्ञाता हो, वह विकारों के हेतु, लिङ्ग और उपशान्ति के विषय में मोहित नहीं होगा।
english: He who knows the gradations (vikalpa) of tastes and knows the gradations of the doṣas would not be confused about the causes, signs and alleviation of disorders.

hindi: द्रव्य का जो रस सूखी अवस्था में और आरम्भ में व्यक्त होता है, वह रस के रूप में लक्षित होता है; इसके विपरीत अनुरस है; क्योंकि सातवाँ रस नहीं है।
english: The taste of a substance that is manifest in it when dry and at the beginning is perceived as the taste (rasa); the subsidiary taste (anurasa) is the opposite; for there is no seventh taste.

text_flags.why: 'rso' (r with no vowel before s) is not a word; rasaḥ (taste) fits the sense, and the half-line then has 16 syllables (15 with rso)

notes: 'at the beginning' (ādau) is taken as the first perception of the taste; 'perceived as the taste' supplies the sense of lakṣyate with rasaḥ. The opposite (viparyayeṇa) is taken as 'not manifest, in the dry state or at the beginning'.

hindi: परत्व और अपरत्व, और युक्ति, संख्या और संयोग, और विभाग, और पृथक्त्व, और परिमाण भी,
english: Remoteness and nearness (paratva and aparatva), rational planning (yukti), number, conjunction, disjunction, separateness and also measure,
notes: SENTENCE: this list has no verb and continues beyond this unit, which is the last of the chunk. parāparatve is a dvandva in the dual (paratva and aparatva), the -tva of the second member serving both. paratva/aparatva may also mean 'superiority and inferiority'; 'remoteness and nearness' is the literal sense. eva in saṃyoga eva ca is a filler emphatic, not translated separately.
